## How these were authored

1. **Fetch first, write second.** Every QID and every expected value was read
   from Wikidata *before* the candidate was written, which is the recorded
   throughput lesson (the author's candidate error rate was about 1 in 4). Two
   instances were changed on the strength of what came back: `mass` was rejected
   for F-SCI-11 because its `P8111` carries two values and would have weakened
   the uniqueness axis 1 tests, and `Panthera` was rejected for F-BIO-11 because
   it records no `P427` at all.
2. **The production path only.** `scripts/benchmark/build_split.py` is a driver
   over the same `semintegrity.benchmark.pilot_builder.build` the pilot uses,
   with `split`/`tier` set for a primary split. No parallel authoring system, and
   probes come from the approved factor design untouched.
3. **A cell with no verifiable interval was not authored.** Seven families have
   their C4 cell outstanding for exactly this reason; an invented P580/P582 was
   never an option.
4. **Negative universals are evidenced positively.** C3 cells use either a
   `claim_cardinality` check (uniqueness) or a zero-count over the registered
   `entities_with_both_properties` query (disjointness), so a NO gold rests on a
   check that succeeds rather than on a check that fails.

## Q27 closure and the suitability hardening — 2026-10-08

Q27 resolved as **Option A**: provider membership unchanged. The 12 exposed
cells (`F-GEO-16`, `F-HIS-11`, `F-HIS-13` — all `official-gazette`) are to be
addressed by **instance selection** toward an approved host that serves the
instrument itself, not by adding hosts. Of `official-gazette`'s three declared
hosts, only `www.gesetze-im-internet.de` serves instruments;
`www.psp.cz` and `alex.onb.ac.at` were both confirmed to serve catalogue pages.

**Suitability gate hardened.** A 1,039-byte JavaScript shell had cleared
`min_document_bytes: 512` and was caught only by a human reading it. An HTML
response must now additionally carry readable text
(`min_html_text_chars: 400`), measured after scripts, styles, comments and tags
are stripped. The rule is on the **representation**, never the provider, and
PDF, XML, JSON and plain text do not reach it. Verified on the real artefact:
`e-sbirka.cz/sb/1992/542` returns 1,040 bytes and **8 characters** of readable
text, and is now refused. Thresholds were chosen from measurement, not taste: a
Cloudflare interstitial yields 16 readable characters; the smallest genuine
document in the study yields about 5,000.

## Corroboration campaign — 2026-10-08. Six attempts, zero attachable, all six diagnosed

Attempted systematically, not assumed infeasible. Every attempt retrieved a real
artefact through the production fetcher.

| # | provider | artefact | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `official-gazette` | `www.psp.cz` Sbírka entry, Act 542/1992 | **catalogue record**, gives the act's effective date (8 Dec 1992), not the dissolution date |
| 2 | `official-gazette` | `aplikace.mvcr.cz` PDF · `e-sbirka.cz` | **404** · **1,040 B shell, 8 chars of text** (now refused by the hardened gate) |
| 3 | `un-treaties` | MTDSG Chapter IV-4, 1,166,562 B, hash-stable | states the **succession** date 1 Jan 1993, not the **dissolution** date |
| 4 | `nasa` | NTRS 19750013242 citation record, Apollo Program Summary Report | abstract says "an 11-year period" — **no dates at all** |
| 5 | `nasa` | NSSDCA `1998-069F` (Unity) | **CONTRADICTS Wikidata**: "Launch Date: 1998-12-13" vs `P619 = 1998-12-04`. The mechanism working as designed |
| 6 | `crossref` | `api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/171737a0` | **the chain passes**: suitable, hash-stable, and states `[[1953,4,25]]` in three machine-readable fields. Blocked only by **Q28** — a sibling claim in the same constraint cites an unmapped host |

**Six distinct blocker classes, now named:** catalogue-not-instrument · adjacent
fact · unmapped citation → `undetermined` · fact buried in PDF prose the approved
tooling is forbidden to extract · source *contradicts* the primary value ·
same-witness. Only one is a policy question (**Q28**); the rest are per-instance
sourcing facts.

**The decisive structural lesson.** Corroboration succeeds only where an approved
provider expresses the needed fact in a **machine-readable field**. That holds for
`crossref` (publication dates), `taxonomic-authority` (JSON records),
`standards-body` (CIAAW tables) and `nasa`/NSSDCA (greppable text) — and fails
for `govinfo`, `national-archives` and most `official-gazette` cells, where the
fact lives in PDF prose. Since corroboration is required precisely for *temporal*
facts, and the machine-readable providers mostly express *non-temporal* ones, the
overlap is narrow. `crossref` publication dates are the one clean intersection.

**Technique added:** `claim_time` verifies only the year. Wikidata's exact time
serialization (`+1947-08-14T00:00:00Z`) compares cleanly through
`claim_literal`, verified against the live API, so axis-4 precedence and axis-6
boundaries are now machine-checked at **day precision**. Three families turn on
events one day apart or on exact dates that a year check could not separate.

### The 26 remaining cells, by cause

**Group A — 14 C4 cells whose underlying fact has no recorded interval.**
A C4 constraint needs a `P580`/`P582` boundary that is machine-checkable. These
facts are atemporal or instantaneous, so authoring one would mean fabricating an
interval:

| cells | why |
|---|---|
| `F-BIO-11`, `F-BIO-12`, `F-BIO-13`, dev `F-BIO-03` C4 | taxonomic placement carries no interval qualifiers |
| `F-SCI-11`, `F-SCI-12`, `F-SCI-15`, `F-GEO-15` C4 | SI base units, periodic-table groups, atomic numbers and summit elevations are atemporal |
| `F-BIO-14`, `F-HIS-14`, `F-SCI-14`, dev `F-SCI-04` C4 | axis-4 events are POINTS (publications, declarations, inventions); no interval exists to bound |
| `F-GEO-12` C4 | `Q750 P31 -> Q123480` carries no qualifiers; Bolivia's 1884 loss of coastline is not recorded as an interval |
| `F-BIO-16` C4 | the species' `P580` is −5,000,000, which `TemporalValidity`'s date field cannot represent |

**Group B — 12 axis-5 cells blocked on an admissible measure.** ADR-0018
requires a measure for **every** member of the universe. Five searches have now
failed:

| family | attempts |
|---|---|
| `F-BIO-15` | mammals (fin whale, elephant, hippo, white rhino — all absent), birds (ostrich 1.5/115/100, emu 581.2/32.7/38.3), reptiles (both crocodiles absent), trees (*Sequoia*, *Eucalyptus regnans* absent), cetaceans (humpback 16/4.5 and 45/1.5 irreconcilable; sperm, bowhead, orca absent) |
| `F-HIS-15`, `F-POL-15` | the measure is a **duration**. Wikidata stores it only as `P580`/`P582` qualifiers on `P39`, and no registered query in `configs/kb/sparql_queries.yaml` ranks by a computed interval. Using one would mean substituting an unregistered measure |

**Neither group is a global blocker.** Group A is a property of the facts the
approved matrix assigned to those families, and Group B needs one decision: accept
axis 5 at 8/20 with the shortfall stated, or extend ADR-0018's admissible measure
sources. Both are recorded, neither was decided here.
